newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan special income tax cut should be stopped-MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan special income tax cut should be stopped-MOF.

text.p: Japanese special income tax cuts should be stopped from next fiscal year, Vice Finance Minister Tadashi Ogawa told a news conference on Thursday.
The special tax cut of two trillion yen for the current fiscal year to March 31 is a measure only for 1996/97 and should not be made next fiscal year, Ogawa said.
Ogawa said the special tax is a distribution of money which comes from the future debt of the government.
"Such a special income tax cut should be stopped as soon as possible," he said.
Ogawa said the special tax was aimed at stimulating the economy but the economic recovery is now more solid than before.
